prerequisites.title: Help Scout account with API access
prerequisites.detail: You need a Help Scout user who can open Your Profile > My apps. The pricing page does not say whether OAuth apps need a specific paid plan.

prerequisites.title: Public HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: The Authorization Code flow needs a redirection URL set when you create the app. Use the callback URL from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in Help Scout
steps.detail: Go to Your Profile > My apps and click Create My App. Enter the redirection URL when prompted.
steps.done_when: You have an application ID and secret.

steps.title: Copy the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Take the callback URL from the Composio dashboard and check it is a public HTTPS address.
steps.done_when: The redirect URI is entered in the Help Scout app.

steps.title: Use a placeholder redirect URL
steps.detail: For Client Credentials only, a placeholder redirect URL is accepted to finish creating the app.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for toolkit help_scout via Composio's API with your application ID and secret.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Authorize with an active, invited Help Scout user and confirm tool calls work.

traps.title: No managed app to prototype with
traps.detail: Composio has no managed Help Scout app, so even prototypes need your own app.

traps.title: Users must be active and invited
traps.detail: Credentials tied to a user who is not active and invited in the account return a 401 error.

traps.title: Sidebar-app rules are different
traps.detail: The admin or account-owner requirement is documented for Inbox sidebar apps, not OAuth apps.

blockers.what_it_means: The credentials do not belong to an active, invited user in the Help Scout account.
blockers.what_to_do: Invite or reactivate the user and reconnect.

evidence.answer: The Publish branding button makes the new branding live.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If your app also requires verification for sensitive or restricted scopes, navigate to the OAuth Verification Center to track your Data access status and provide any additional information requested, such as a demonstration video.
evidence.answer: For sensitive or restricted scopes, the developer navigates to the OAuth Verification Center to track data access status and provide requested information such as a demonstration video.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If any of your OAuth clients aren't ready for production, we suggest that you delete them from the project that's requesting verification.
evidence.answer: OAuth clients not ready for production should be deleted from the project requesting verification, using the Clients page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For example, a project can contain one or more OAuth clients, configure APIs for use by those clients, and configure an OAuth consent screen that's shown to users before they authorize access to your app.
evidence.answer: A Cloud Console project can contain one or more OAuth clients and an OAuth consent screen shown to users before they authorize the app.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You must limit your use of Google user data to the practices that your published privacy policy discloses.
evidence.answer: Google user data must only be used as disclosed in the app's published privacy policy.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You must request the narrowest scope necessary for your app's functionality and ensure data usage complies with API policies and your privacy policy.
evidence.answer: Data use must comply with API policies and the app's privacy policy.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Just need the basics? The Free plan includes 5 users, 1 Inbox, and 1 Docs site.
evidence.answer: Help Scout has a Free plan, and paid plans start at Standard at $25 per user/mo; the pricing page does not say API or OAuth app access requires a specific paid plan, though its comparison table lists a 'Webhooks & OAuth apps' row.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Help Scout implements OAuth 2.0 but publishes no discrete scopes
evidence.answer: Per this third-party scope catalog (not Help Scout's official docs), Help Scout exposes no per-scope OAuth consent, so no scope tier appears to trigger extra review; this is unverified against official docs.
